feedback: The candidate retains the same geometry and sensor layout as the previous iteration, which was well balanced and effective. The controller gains have been adjusted from the previous iteration: the derivative gain kd is reduced from 3 to 1.5, the integral gain ki from 0.5 to 0.2, and the base speed from 1.5 to 1.3. These changes are based on the earlier race data (iteration 0) showing no line loss events and good completion but some steering oscillation likely caused by the high kd. The reduced kd and ki should reduce oscillations and integral windup, improving stability. The slightly lower base speed aims to prevent stalling and maintain control. The sensor weights and line loss strategy remain unchanged, as they were effective. The requested observations continue to cover completion, progress, errors, line loss events, steering oscillation, and control effort to monitor the impact of these changes. Depending on the next race results, if oscillations persist, consider further lowering kd or adjusting sensor weights; if the robot stalls or slows excessively, consider increasing base speed slightly or tuning ki. If line loss events occur, consider changing the line_loss strategy or sensor layout.
